biblical_reference.note: In the New Testament, the name Peter (Greek: Πέτρος, Petros) is given to the apostle Simon Bar-Jonah, who was a fisherman by trade before Jesus called him to be a disciple. Peter was a key figure among the apostles and is traditionally considered to be the first Bishop of Rome and the founder of the Roman Catholic Church.

saint_reference.note: Saint Peter, also known as Simon Peter or Peter of Bethsaida, was a fisherman by trade before Jesus called him to be a disciple. He is considered the first Pope and the founder of the Roman Catholic Church. He is traditionally regarded as a saint in many Christian denominations and is venerated as a patron saint of fishermen, travelers, and those in need of forgiveness.

data.cultural_impact: The name Petr, with its roots in Latin, links the bearer to the rich history and cultural influence of Rome and the Roman Catholic Church. With the name Petr, comes the legacy of Saint Peter, a symbol of leadership and the foundation of the Church.

He is considered to be the rock upon which Christ built his Church and is a symbol of unwavering faith and commitment to God. The name Petr reminding us of the spiritual strength and foundation that comes from our faith in God.
